raw_response:
1. The figure shows no error bars at all—only bar lengths for counts—so it doesn’t provide evidence about variability in task performance within IE-Slavic versus IE-Romance.

2. IE-Germanic has about 44–45 tasks, while Uralic has about 20, so IE-Germanic is a bit more than double. A likely explanation is simply that the dataset includes more tasks/languages from IE-Germanic than from Uralic, but the chart itself doesn’t state why.

3. The chart provides only counts and no underlying sample sizes/variance or statistical test setup, so a p-value can’t be computed from it. It does show IE-Slavic (~79) has more tasks than IE-Romance (~47), indicating a clear difference in representation, but “statistical significance” isn’t available here.
